executive_summary: Drop 23 confirmed-dead backup/snapshot tables that were publicly readable via the anon key with zero row-level protection, permanently removing roughly 13,000 of the ~15,356 exposed rows the chairman's own Advisors security scan flagged. Chairman-approved (ratification 49686fd3, verbatim 'approve the drops'). The migration was already authored, chairman-approved, committed and applied to the live database (independently re-verified via a direct pg connection to information_schema: 0/23 tables present) before this PRD was written; this PRD formalizes the already-executed, already-safety-verified work through the LEO protocol for a clean audit trail. The 13 remaining live tables with the same exposure, and key rotation, are explicitly out of scope -- reserved as separate follow-up work needing per-table triage.

functional_requirements.title: Drop the 23 chairman-approved dead-snapshot tables
functional_requirements.description: database/migrations/20260915_close_public_read_drop_dead_snapshots.sql drops exactly the 23 tables named in chairman_drop_approval.scope_exactly (the qparity20260610 parity-run snapshots, the storm-quarantine snapshot, and the sd_baseline_items backup/recon snapshots). No FK references any of them; each is confirmed a stale partial duplicate of a live, populated source table. Already applied to the live database; independently re-verified via a direct pg connection to information_schema.tables (0/23 present).

functional_requirements.title: Re-verify the drop's effect via a connection method immune to PostgREST schema-cache staleness
functional_requirements.description: Post-DDL verification must use a direct pg connection (scripts/lib/supabase-connection.js createDatabaseClient querying information_schema.tables) rather than the Supabase-js client, which can serve a stale PostgREST schema cache immediately after DDL applied through a different connection path -- a trap both this session and the coordinator's own earlier verification pass independently hit and resolved the same way.

functional_requirements.title: Explicitly exclude the 13 live tables and key rotation from this SD's scope
functional_requirements.description: The 13 live tables carrying the same public-read exposure (door_routing_ledger, scope_completion_chain, north_star, selection_postures, venture_experience_review_runs, coverage_matrix, coverage_matrix_rotation_runs, sourcing_chairman_queue, v_id, claim_rejects, venture_preview_instances, v_hc_flag_enabled, v_s22_flag_enabled) need per-table row-level-security decisions, not removal -- some may be deliberately public for a dashboard. Key rotation is also excluded, deliberately sequenced after DB work since rotating the project secret invalidates the service-role key every live fleet seat currently uses. Both are reserved as separate, later follow-up work, not decided or implemented by this SD.

acceptance_criteria: A direct pg-connection query against information_schema.tables for all 23 table names returns 0 rows.
No foreign-key constraint anywhere in the live schema references any of the 23 dropped table names.
The migration file carries the chairman-approval provenance trail (ratification id, verbatim quote, approver) in its header, matching the repo's established chairman-gated migration convention.

test_scenarios.description: Direct pg-connection query (bypassing PostgREST/Supabase-js, which can serve a stale schema cache after DDL) against information_schema.tables for all 23 names -- expect 0 rows.
Confirm the migration file's DROP TABLE statement list matches chairman_drop_approval.scope_exactly exactly (23 names, no extras, no omissions).

components.name: database/migrations/20260915_close_public_read_drop_dead_snapshots.sql
components.description: Chairman-gated DDL migration dropping the 23 dead snapshot tables. Already applied to the live database.

phases.description: Migration authored, chairman-approved, committed, and applied to the live database before this SD's formal LEO protocol pass began.
Independent re-verification via a direct pg connection (not Supabase-js/PostgREST, which can read stale post-DDL) that all 23 tables are genuinely absent.

risks.risk: A Supabase-js/PostgREST-based check can read a stale schema cache immediately after DDL applied via a direct pg connection, producing a false 'still exists' result.
risks.mitigation: Any future re-verification of this migration's effect should use a direct pg connection to information_schema, not the Supabase-js client -- documented in this SD's own metadata as a caught, resolved trap.

consumers: None -- the 23 dropped tables had no live consumers (confirmed dead by the same triage that recommended dropping them).
dependencies: Live source tables for each dropped snapshot remain populated and unaffected.
data_contracts: No schema change to any live table; only the 23 dead tables are removed.
observability_rollout: Already applied and verified; no phased rollout needed for a completed DROP TABLE migration.
